Subject: Light Up a Life 2026

Yes, Hilary, we are doing the tree. Hilary asked on here last week, and I expect she isn't the only one wondering, so here is everything in one place.

Our Light Up a Life tree will be in the shop window again this year. Memory tags will be on the counter from Monday 16 November. The suggested donation is £3. If you would rather write your tag quietly at home, there are envelopes on the counter too, so you can take one away and bring it back when you're ready.

The tree goes into the window on Saturday 28 November, and we'll switch the lights on that afternoon at 4pm. The Gildencroft Primary choir are kindly coming back to sing three or four carols. Doreen is doing her mince pies again, and I'd advise you to arrive in good time, given what happened to them last year.

Every name on every tag will be read out at the hospice remembrance service on Sunday 13 December at 3pm, in the day centre. You are very welcome to come, but you don't have to. Your person's name will be read either way.

I'd like to say a couple of things this year that I don't always manage to say.

The tree is for anyone who is missing someone. You don't need to have had anyone at the hospice. If you've lost a husband, a mum, a friend from work or the neighbour who always took your parcels in, there is room for them on our tree.

You also don't need to buy a tag, or buy anything at all. If you're passing and you'd simply like to stand by the tree for a minute, please come in and do that. Nobody will ask you any questions, and you can stay as long as you like. There is a stool behind the counter if your legs need it, and the kettle is never far away.

It's seven years this month since my husband Ray died at the hospice. The first year I hung his tag I could hardly write it. I stood at the counter for an age with the pen in my hand and, in the end, someone else had to help me with the string. Now I write it at the same counter, with the same pen, and it takes no time at all. I don't say that to suggest it all gets easy, because it doesn't. But it does change, and the tree has been part of that for me. I suspect I'm not alone. When I take the tags down each January I read a good many of them, and they are full of love and quite often very funny.

Thank you to everyone who came last year. You squeezed into Magdalen Street in the cold, sang along whether or not you knew the words, and between you put 412 names on that tree. Every one of them was somebody's somebody. I think about that every time I walk past the window.

So do come in from the 16th, or come and see the lights go on on the 28th, or just come and stand by the tree whenever you need to. We'll be here, Tuesday to Saturday, 10 till 4.

With love,
Jean
